lessons.title: Microsoft Entra ID functions and identity types
lessons.summary: Explore Microsoft Entra ID as a cloud identity service and learn how users, groups, devices, workload identities, external identities, and hybrid identity fit together.
learningObjectives: Describe Microsoft Entra ID as a cloud identity provider
Distinguish users, groups, devices, workload, and external identities
Identify when hybrid identity connects on-premises and cloud directories
Choose the right identity type for common access scenarios
lessons.explanation:
Relecloud has employees, contractors, laptops, and automation scripts. Treating all of them as the same kind of account would be messy and risky. **Microsoft Entra ID** is Microsoft's cloud identity and access service that helps organizations manage identities, sign-ins, access to apps, and directory objects.

A **user** identity normally represents a person. A **group** collects users, devices, or other objects so access can be assigned consistently. A **device** identity represents an endpoint that can be registered, joined, managed, and evaluated by access policies. A **workload identity** represents an application, service, or automation that needs to access resources without being a person. External identities support collaboration with guests and partners.

Many organizations also have on-premises directory services. **Hybrid identity** connects on-premises identity investments with Microsoft Entra ID so users can access cloud apps while the organization manages a combined identity environment. In the **Manage users, groups, and directory roles in Microsoft Entra** lab, you practise this mental model by creating a user, organizing access with a group, and assigning a least-privileged directory role.

lessons.businessScenario: Relecloud creates a workforce user for Alex, adds Alex to the Field Technicians group, registers a company tablet, invites a supplier as an external identity, and creates a workload identity for an inventory sync app.
lessons.technicalExample: Example access plan: `Field Technicians group -> Inventory app user access`; `InventorySync workload identity -> application permission to read stock API`; `Supplier guest -> time-bound project group`.

misconception.myth: A workload identity is just a shared user account with a password.
misconception.reality: A workload identity represents an app or service and should be managed separately from human user accounts.

lessons.examTakeaway: Look for clues: people are users, collections are groups, endpoints are devices, apps and automation are workload identities, and on-premises plus cloud is hybrid identity.
lessons.recap: Microsoft Entra ID provides the cloud directory and sign-in foundation for many Microsoft and custom applications.
lessons.simplerExplanation: Think of a building directory: people, teams, visitor badges, equipment badges, and service robots are different entries with different rules.
lessons.anotherExample: A university uses Microsoft Entra ID for students and staff, invites a partner researcher as an external identity, and uses a workload identity for a nightly roster import.

lessons.title: Authentication methods and password protection
lessons.summary: Learn how Microsoft Entra authentication methods, MFA, passwordless options, self-service password reset, and password protection improve sign-in security.
learningObjectives: Compare passwords, MFA, passwordless sign-in, and SSPR
Describe how password protection blocks weak or banned passwords
Identify authentication methods that strengthen user sign-in
Choose MFA or passwordless options for sign-in security scenarios
lessons.explanation:
Alpine Ski House wants sign-ins to be secure without turning every Monday morning into a help desk queue. Microsoft Entra ID supports several **authentication methods** so organizations can move beyond a single reusable password. **Multifactor authentication (MFA)** asks for two or more factors, such as something the user knows and something the user has.

**Passwordless authentication** removes the typed password from the sign-in flow, using methods such as authenticator-based approvals or security keys depending on configuration. **Self-service password reset (SSPR)** lets users reset or unlock accounts after proving their identity with registered methods, reducing help desk tickets. **Password protection** helps block weak, common, or organization-specific banned passwords.

Authentication is also a great place to connect lessons to labs. The **Require MFA with a Conditional Access policy** lab lets you practise a report-only policy that requires MFA while excluding emergency access accounts. That lab is about access policy, but the user experience depends on the authentication methods configured here.

terminology.definition: A way an identity proves itself during sign-in or reset.
Authentication using two or more different verification factors.
A sign-in approach that avoids typing a reusable password.
A capability that lets users reset or unlock accounts after verification.
Controls that help block weak, common, or banned passwords.

lessons.businessScenario: Alpine Ski House pilots passwordless sign-in for store managers, enables SSPR for employees, and blocks passwords containing the company name or seasonal phrases.
lessons.technicalExample: Rollout checklist: `1. Pilot with IT`, `2. Require registration`, `3. Enable SSPR for a target group`, `4. Use Conditional Access to require MFA`, `5. Monitor feedback`.

misconception.myth: MFA and passwordless authentication are the same thing.
misconception.reality: MFA describes using multiple factors. Passwordless describes removing the typed password.

lessons.examTakeaway: When a scenario asks about a second verification prompt, think MFA. For help desk password resets, think SSPR. To block weak passwords, think password protection.
lessons.recap: Microsoft Entra authentication capabilities reduce reliance on passwords and help users recover accounts safely.
lessons.simplerExplanation: A password is like one house key. MFA adds a second check, SSPR is a verified locksmith process, and password protection refuses flimsy keys.
lessons.anotherExample: Northwind Traders enables SSPR and password protection, then pilots passwordless sign-in for managers who use shared shop devices.

modules.summary: Covers Conditional Access, roles, RBAC, ID Protection, access reviews, entitlement management, and Privileged Identity Management.

lessons.title: Access management with Conditional Access and roles
lessons.summary: Understand how Conditional Access evaluates sign-in signals and how Microsoft Entra roles and RBAC support least-privileged administration.
learningObjectives: Explain how Conditional Access uses signals to make access decisions
Identify user, location, device, app, and risk signals in policies
Distinguish Microsoft Entra roles from resource RBAC permissions
Choose least-privileged role assignments for administration tasks
lessons.explanation:
Fabrikam's finance app is not sensitive only when people are in the office. Risk depends on who signs in, from where, on what device, to which app, and under what risk conditions. **Microsoft Entra Conditional Access** is the policy engine that brings these signals together and applies controls such as requiring MFA, blocking access, or requiring a compliant device.

Access management also includes administrative permissions. **Microsoft Entra roles** are permission sets for directory tasks, such as managing users or applications. **Role-based access control (RBAC)** assigns permissions through roles so administrators do not receive broad rights they do not need. Least privilege means choosing the role and scope that match the job, then reviewing it later.

Two labs make this concrete. In **Manage users, groups, and directory roles in Microsoft Entra**, you assign a least-privileged role. In **Require MFA with a Conditional Access policy**, you practise targeting a policy to require MFA while protecting emergency access accounts.

terminology.definition: A Microsoft Entra policy engine that evaluates signals and applies access controls.
Information such as user, location, device, app, or risk used in an access decision.
A requirement or action such as require MFA, block access, or require compliant device.
A directory permission set used for administrative tasks.
Assigning permissions through roles instead of one-off permissions.
Granting only the access needed to perform a task.

lessons.businessScenario: Fabrikam requires MFA for finance app sign-ins from outside trusted locations and gives the help desk the User Administrator role instead of Global Administrator.
lessons.technicalExample: Conditional Access sketch: `Assignments: Finance group + Payroll app`; `Conditions: Outside trusted locations`; `Grant: Require multifactor authentication`; `Mode: Report-only pilot before enforcement`.

misconception.myth: Conditional Access is only an MFA switch.
misconception.reality: MFA is one common grant control, but Conditional Access evaluates multiple signals and can apply different controls or block access.

lessons.examTakeaway: Location, device, app, user, group, and risk point to Conditional Access; administrator task permissions point to Microsoft Entra roles and RBAC.
lessons.recap: Access management combines dynamic sign-in policies with least-privileged administration.
lessons.simplerExplanation: Conditional Access is like a smart building guard who checks badge, time, location, device condition, and room sensitivity before deciding whether to allow entry.
lessons.anotherExample: A retailer blocks legacy sign-ins to finance tools, requires MFA for managers outside the country, and assigns the Groups Administrator role only to the team that manages membership.

lessons.title: Identity protection and governance
lessons.summary: Learn how Microsoft Entra ID Protection, access reviews, entitlement management, and Privileged Identity Management reduce identity risk and control access over time.
learningObjectives: Describe how ID Protection detects risky users and sign-ins
Identify access reviews that remove unneeded permissions
Explain how entitlement management packages access for users
Choose PIM for just-in-time privileged role activation
lessons.explanation:
Contoso's project access problem is not only, 'Can people sign in today?' It is also, 'Should they still have access next month, and should admins hold powerful roles all the time?' Microsoft Entra includes protection and governance capabilities for that lifecycle.

**Microsoft Entra ID Protection** detects identity risks such as risky users and sign-ins and can support investigation and remediation. **Microsoft Entra ID Governance** helps organizations balance productivity and security by managing who should have access, why, and for how long. **Access reviews** periodically ask reviewers or users to confirm whether access is still needed. **Entitlement management** packages access to groups, apps, and sites with request, approval, and lifecycle controls. **Privileged Identity Management (PIM)** helps manage privileged roles with eligible assignments, activation requirements, approvals, and auditing.

The **Configure an eligible role assignment in Privileged Identity Management** lab is the hands-on companion: you practise just-in-time eligibility, require MFA and approval for activation, and audit a simulated activation request.

terminology.definition: A capability for detecting, investigating, and helping remediate identity-based risk.
Microsoft Entra capabilities for managing identity lifecycle and access governance.
A process to periodically confirm whether users should keep access.
Governance for access packages that bundle resources, request policies, and approvals.
A capability for managing, activating, and auditing privileged role access.
A role assignment that can be activated when needed instead of remaining active all the time.

lessons.businessScenario: Contoso creates an access package for a merger project, requires manager approval, schedules access reviews every quarter, and makes the Security Administrator role eligible through PIM.
lessons.technicalExample: Governance flow: `Create access package -> User requests access -> Approver reviews -> User receives time-bound access -> Access review checks ongoing need -> PIM handles privileged elevation`.

misconception.myth: Governance is only useful after a breach.
misconception.reality: Governance is preventive and ongoing. It helps ensure people get appropriate access, keep it only while needed, and use privileged roles safely.

lessons.examTakeaway: Risky sign-ins point to ID Protection. Periodic confirmation points to access reviews. Packaged approvals point to entitlement management. Just-in-time admin roles point to PIM.
lessons.recap: Identity protection detects risk; governance controls access lifecycle; PIM limits standing privilege.
lessons.simplerExplanation: Access is like a library card. ID Protection spots suspicious use, entitlement management issues the right card, access reviews check continued need, and PIM keeps the master key locked until approved use.
lessons.anotherExample: A hospital grants temporary app access to visiting researchers through an access package, reviews membership monthly, and requires PIM approval before activating privileged roles.
